set.n: Conrad May's two iron pots (~$50,000), buried in Grant County near Louisburg (1897; find denied)
set.v: About $50,000 in bills and gold in two iron pots (his own 1897 statement)
set.st: Conrad May, sued for alimony, was examined before Referee N. E. Utt in Sep 1897 (Dubuque Times, via the Lancaster Teller): he said he had sold one Grant Co farm for $12,000 and another for over $20,000 and, with other money, 'had buried it in two pots under the ground', nearly $50,000 in bills and gold in two iron pots, somewhere in Grant County within a dozen miles of Dubuque. He refused to say where, and the referee would not compel him, fearing a rush 'greater than to the Klondike'. Jailed at Dubuque, he paid alimony rather than reveal the spot; the Grant County Herald said he 'has had his wealth buried in the southern part of Grant county'. In Oct 1897 the Dubuque Times said a neighbour's dog turned it up in a gopher hole, and the "find" was "the reigning sensation in Dickeyville". A week later the Cuba City News investigated and denied the Times' account. Nothing was shown recovered. Pin is on the c.1915 plat house mark of his old farm, not the spot itself.
set.t: Two period accounts, including May's own refusal to reveal the spot, say the money was buried; the only 'find' was denied a week later and nothing was shown recovered. He had sold both farms by Jan 1897 (544 acres, to his brother Herman), so the pots may lie on the old farms or elsewhere within a dozen miles of Dubuque. Private farmland: permission.
set.tovw: C: two 1897 period accounts (Grant Co Herald; Dubuque Times via Lancaster Teller) of a buried, unrecovered sum; spot unstated; find denied.
pinev: Farm-level: the c.1915 Hixson Grant plat (Jamestown p.94) shows 361 ac of May land in the S/W part of sec 12 T1N R2W, the section that holds Louisburg (GNIS 42.5792,-90.5557); house mark about 400 m S of Louisburg. Whether this is the 1897 farm is not proven (about 600 m).

1895 Grant Co plat, Jamestown T1N R2W p. 60 (Ancestry image 31617_072128-00173): 'Conrad May 521' in sec 12 S of Louisburg P.O.; 1900 census Conrad and Louisa May, Jamestown. So the c.1915 house mark is his farm of 1897.
1897: the 180- and 364-acre farms were re-deeded to Herman May in Feb 1897; the 1895 'Conrad May 521' tract is the same land; the pot spot is not stated, hence r1200 and pinconf C.
